title: Cyber defamation - how it differs from regular defamation
p1:
One angry post can travel faster than any rumor ever could. But is an online insult treated the same way as a spoken accusation in a private conversation?

Many people assume defamation is only about what someone says. The digital world has changed the way harmful statements spread.
p2:
A surprising fact: cyber defamation is not a completely separate idea from regular defamation. It is defamation that happens through digital platforms like social media, emails, websites, or online forums.

The biggest difference is reach and permanence. A false statement shared online can be copied, saved, searched, and seen by thousands of people long after it was posted.
p3:
Regular defamation often involves a limited audience, while cyber defamation can grow within minutes. A single comment, review, or post may affect someone's reputation, career, or business.

The practical lesson: think before sharing claims about others online. A delete button does not always erase the damage once information spreads.
conclusion: Have you ever seen an online post or comment that you believe damaged someone's reputation? What made it different from ordinary gossip?
